strings.checkpoint.projectCheckpoints.beforeEver: Before every message you send (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Antigravity), AntiGem saves a hidden copy of the project's files. Each message then gets a restore point: go back to before it, with a preview of every file that changes. Your own git history, branches, staging and stashes are never touched.

strings.checkpoint.projectCheckpoints.oldCheckpo: Old checkpoints are removed automatically (the oldest first when a project uses too much space). Deleting old ones never breaks newer ones: each checkpoint is complete on its own.

strings.checkpoint.projectCheckpoints.onlyFilesI: Only files inside the project go back. Packages the agent installed, files outside the project, servers it started or things it sent are not undone.
strings.checkpoint.projectCheckpoints.filesYourG: Files your .gitignore ignores (and node_modules, .gradle, caches) are not saved and never changed by a restore.
strings.checkpoint.projectCheckpoints.aRestoreFi: A restore first saves the files as they are, so “Undo restore” always works.
strings.checkpoint.projectCheckpoints.goingBackI: Going back in a chat (Edit) only changes the chat. Files go back only through a restore point.

strings.jarvis.panel.noAgentPickedSettingsJarvis: No agent picked: Settings → Jarvis → Agent
strings.jarvis.panel.tapTheOrbAndTalkOr: Tap the orb and talk, or type below. Try “what's running?”, “start a task to fix the failing tests”, “switch to dark mode”, “how do I add an MCP server?”.
strings.jarvis.quickSettings.appliesFromTheNextT: Applies from the next time the microphone opens
strings.jarvis.quickSettings.whatYouSayIsSentAft: What you say is sent after the pause below. Tap Wait on the card to keep talking.
strings.jarvis.quickSettings.nothingIsSentWhileY: Nothing is sent while you think. Tap Send, press the headset button, or say one of your send phrases.
strings.jarvis.quickSettings.longerWhenYouSoundU: Longer when you sound unfinished (“…and”), shorter for short answers.
strings.jarvis.quickSettings.whenITalkWhileJarvi: When I talk while Jarvis works
strings.jarvis.quickSettings.tapToShowOrHideA: Tap to show or hide a switch in the Jarvis panel.
strings.jarvis.service.handsFreeCouldntStartAndr: Hands-free couldn't start: Android doesn't let AntiGem open the microphone from the background. Open AntiGem and turn it on again.
strings.jarvis.service.shownWhileJarvisListensFo: Shown while Jarvis listens for your voice
strings.jarvis.settings.offChatOnlyNoFloatingBut: Off = chat only: no floating button, no microphone, nothing read out loud. You use Jarvis in the Jarvis chats you open from the chat list (Jarvis tab → New Jarvis chat), by typing.
strings.jarvis.settings.tapTheOrbToTalkLong: Tap the orb to talk, long-press it for the Jarvis panel (tasks, conversation, typing, quick switches). You can also type to Jarvis: Jarvis tab in the chat list → New Jarvis chat.
strings.jarvis.settings.chatOnlyOpenTheJarvisTab: Chat only: open the Jarvis tab in the chat list and tap “New Jarvis chat”. Pick its agent and model like in any chat.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisChatsInTheChatList: Jarvis chats in the chat list
strings.jarvis.settings.myJarvisChatsInAllToo: My Jarvis chats in All too
strings.jarvis.settings.allJarvisChatsInAllToo: All Jarvis chats in All too
strings.jarvis.settings.everyJarvisChatTheVoiceC: Every Jarvis chat, the voice chats Jarvis opens by itself too, also shows in All and the agent tabs.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisChatsAreListedOnly: Jarvis chats are listed only under the Jarvis tab. The work chats Jarvis starts for its tasks are normal chats and always show in All.
strings.jarvis.settings.pickTheAgentJarvisTalksT: Pick the agent Jarvis talks to. Nothing is selected yet, so Jarvis can't answer.
strings.jarvis.settings.agenttitleIsTurnedOffInS: {agentTitle} is turned off in Settings → Agents: turn it on, or pick another agent here.
strings.jarvis.settings.theGrammaticalGenderJarv: The grammatical gender Jarvis uses for itself. It matters in languages like Hindi (“main kar rahi hoon” / “main kar raha hoon”). Pick a matching voice under Voice output.
strings.jarvis.settings.eGCallMeSantoshReply: e.g. Call me Santosh. Reply in Hinglish. I mostly work on the antigem project.
strings.jarvis.settings.sentWithTheFirstMessageO: Sent with the first message of every new Jarvis chat. When you change it (or the persona), the open chat is told with your next message. Jarvis' own memory note (Settings → Jarvis → Jarvis chat) is separate: Jarvis edits that one itself.
strings.jarvis.settings.pickTheAgentJarvisTalksT: Pick the agent Jarvis talks to first (Settings → Jarvis → Agent).
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisReportedThatItsApp: Jarvis reported that its app tools are missing in {agentTitle}. Add the Jarvis MCP server below (then start a fresh Jarvis chat).
strings.jarvis.settings.requiredTheseAreTheTools: Required: these are the tools Jarvis controls the app with.
strings.jarvis.settings.n2LetJarvisToolsRunWitho: 2. Let Jarvis' tools run without asking
strings.jarvis.settings.otherwiseEverySpokenAnsw: Otherwise every spoken answer would need an approval.
strings.jarvis.settings.notNeededTheGuideGoesWit: Not needed: the guide goes with the first message.
strings.jarvis.settings.theFirstMessageOfEveryJa: The first message of every Jarvis chat carries the whole guide and the list of its tools with their parameters, so the model acts at once instead of searching. If the Jarvis MCP server is missing, Jarvis says so and this card shows a warning.
strings.jarvis.settings.heyJarvisOpenMyProjectSt: “Hey Jarvis, open my project” starts right away. Common mishearings of “Jarvis” count too. The wake phrase needs hands-free mode and keeps the device recognizer busy, which uses battery.
strings.jarvis.settings.keepsJarvisMicrophoneSer: Keeps Jarvis' microphone service running so the wake phrase and the headset button work with the screen off or another app open. A notification shows its state with Talk / Send / Stop.
strings.jarvis.settings.withHandsFreeOnOnePress: With hands-free on: one press talks (or sends), two presses stop. Works while no music app holds the button.
strings.jarvis.settings.quickSettingsTilePullDow: Quick Settings tile: pull down the notification shade, edit the tiles and add “Jarvis” to talk from anywhere with one tap. While AntiGem runs in the background it listens without opening the app.
strings.jarvis.settings.alsoLongPressTheAntigemI: Also: long-press the AntiGem icon → Jarvis, or put Jarvis on the home screen.
strings.jarvis.settings.thisLauncherCantAddShort: This launcher can't add shortcuts. Long-press the AntiGem icon instead.
strings.jarvis.settings.youCanAlwaysSendWithThe: You can always send with the Send button on the card, the headset button or the notification's Send.
strings.jarvis.settings.offNothingIsSentWhileYou: Off: nothing is sent while you take a break to think. Say a send phrase or tap Send when you're done.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisWaitsLongerWhenYou: Jarvis waits longer when you sound unfinished (“…and”, “…the”) and less for short answers. Tap Wait to keep talking.
strings.jarvis.settings.whenJarvisJustAskedYouSo: When Jarvis just asked you something, your answer is sent after the pause above, even with auto send off.
strings.jarvis.settings.answersAreSentExactlyLik: Answers are sent exactly like everything else. The send mode is fixed when the microphone opens and never changes while you talk.
strings.jarvis.settings.endWithOneOfTheseAnd: End with one of these and it is sent at once (the phrase itself is not sent).
strings.jarvis.settings.endWithOneOfTheseAnd2: End with one of these and nothing is sent.
strings.jarvis.settings.aPhraseOnlyCountsAtThe: A phrase only counts at the very end. “…and send it”, “…to send it”, “can you do it” and “don't send it” stay part of your message. Short or everyday phrases (“send”, “over”, “do it”) only count when you say them on their own after a short pause. When a phrase keeps firing by mistake, remove it or add a longer sentence instead (e.g. “jarvis send it now”).
strings.jarvis.settings.afterJarvisSpeaksListenF: After Jarvis speaks, listen for your reply
strings.jarvis.settings.theMicrophoneOpensAfterE: The microphone opens after every answer while you are talking to Jarvis.
strings.jarvis.settings.theMicrophoneOnlyOpensWh: The microphone only opens when you tap or wake Jarvis (and when it asks you something it needs right away).
strings.jarvis.settings.ifYouSayNothingAtAll: If you say nothing at all in this time, the microphone closes with a soft tone.
strings.jarvis.settings.duringFollowUpListeningJ: During follow-up listening Jarvis only reacts when you say its name (or answer its question).
During follow-up listening Jarvis ignores what was clearly said to someone else, and filler like “um”.
strings.jarvis.settings.speakingWhileJarvisIsSti: Speaking while Jarvis is still working
strings.jarvis.settings.tonesWhenTheMicrophoneOp: Tones when the microphone opens and closes
strings.jarvis.settings.thisDeviceUsesAndroidsRe: “This device” uses Android's recognizer and needs no sign-in. If the agent's dictation fails, Jarvis switches to the device for the rest of the session.
strings.jarvis.settings.yourOwnPhrasesThatActAt: Your own phrases that act at once, without asking the model, when you say them on their own (optionally with “Jarvis” or “please”). There are none until you add them, so a plain “okay” or “stop” in a conversation always goes to Jarvis like anything else.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisShowsItsAnswersOnT: Jarvis shows its answers on the card instead of saying them (meetings, night). Also in quick settings (tune icon).
strings.jarvis.settings.ifTheOnlineVoiceFailsJar: If the online voice fails, Jarvis falls back to this device's voice.
strings.jarvis.settings.helloImJarvisThisIsHow: Hello, I'm Jarvis. This is how I sound.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisSaysAShortLineWhil: Jarvis says a short line while a long step runs.
strings.jarvis.settings.youCanAlsoSaySpeakSlower: You can also say “speak slower”, “faster” or “repeat that”: Jarvis handles those at once, without asking the model.
strings.jarvis.settings.sayBuildTheReleaseAndTel: Say “build the release and tell me when it's done”: Jarvis starts a task in its own chat and watches it. You can ask how it is going, redirect it (“also run the tests”), stop it, or answer its questions by voice. Tasks are listed in the Jarvis panel.
strings.jarvis.settings.whenATaskFinishesFailsOr: When a task finishes, fails or gets stuck
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisReadsTheResultTell: Jarvis reads the result, tells you the gist and follows up (asks you, passes answers on). Uses a model turn per event.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisJustAnnouncesItRel: Jarvis just announces it (“Release build is done”), without a model turn.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisApprovesWhatClearl: Jarvis approves what clearly serves the task's goal and asks you about anything risky or unclear (needs “Jarvis decides” above).
strings.jarvis.settings.approvalsFollowApprovals: Approvals follow “Approvals by voice” below: approved automatically or read out to you.
strings.jarvis.settings.reportATaskWithNoProgres: Report a task with no progress after
strings.jarvis.settings.sayWhenAnyOtherChatFinis: Say when any other chat finishes
strings.jarvis.settings.chatTitleIsDonePleaseChe: “<chat title> is done. Please check it.” for chats that are not Jarvis tasks.
strings.jarvis.settings.notForTheChatImLooking: Not for the chat I'm looking at
strings.jarvis.settings.alsoReadTheStartOfThe: Also read the start of the reply
strings.jarvis.settings.forAnnouncementsWithoutA: For announcements without a model turn.
strings.jarvis.settings.warnWhenThe5HourUsage: Warn when the 5-hour usage is almost gone
strings.jarvis.settings.oncePerWindowAtAbout15: Once per window, at about 15% left (Claude Code).
strings.jarvis.settings.openTheJarvisTabInThe: Open the Jarvis tab in the chat list and tap “New Jarvis chat” to type to Jarvis like in any chat. Give it a big job: it writes a mission (goal, done-when, steps), creates teams of agents (e.g. builders and reviewers), hands out tasks in parallel, checks what comes back and keeps going. The strip above the input shows the mission, the teams' tasks and the switches below.
strings.jarvis.settings.readRepliesOutLoudInNew: Read replies out loud in new Jarvis chats
strings.jarvis.settings.whenJarvisSleepsOrPollsW: When Jarvis sleeps or polls while waiting for its tasks
strings.jarvis.settings.stopItHandItTheNews: Stop it, hand it the news
strings.jarvis.settings.noGuardNewsWaitsUntilJar: No guard: news waits until Jarvis ends its turn by itself.
strings.jarvis.settings.whateverComesInMeanwhile: Whatever comes in meanwhile, and everything that finished while Jarvis was busy, goes to it together in one message.
strings.jarvis.settings.withAutopilotOnJarvisIsN: With autopilot on, Jarvis is nudged to continue whenever it stops while the mission is unfinished and nothing runs. Nudges in a row without progress pause it.
strings.jarvis.settings.whetherJarvisChatsAlsoSh: Whether Jarvis chats also show in All: Settings → Jarvis, “Jarvis chats in the chat list”.
strings.jarvis.settings.everythingIsApprovedExce: Everything is approved except risky actions (deleting, pushing, installing from the web), which are read out first.
strings.jarvis.settings.nothingIsAskedUseOnlyIf: Nothing is asked. Use only if you fully trust what the agents do.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisReadsEachRequestOu: Jarvis reads each request out (“It wants to run the command…”) and waits for your yes or no.
strings.jarvis.settings.agentsWillRunCommandsEdi: Agents will run commands, edit files and delete things without asking, including by mistake. Only choose this if you accept that.
strings.jarvis.settings.whileItsActiveWhileJarvi: “While it's active”: while Jarvis listens, works or speaks, or a task runs. Running chats of both agents keep the screen on anyway.
strings.jarvis.settings.dragTheOrbAnywhereItRest: Drag the orb anywhere: it rests on the nearest edge. “Hidden” shows it only while Jarvis is active (use the tile, headset or wake phrase).
strings.jarvis.settings.outsideAntigemTheOrbFloa: Outside AntiGem the orb floats over any app: tap it to talk, long-press it for the Jarvis panel. While Jarvis listens or speaks, its card shows at the bottom of the screen. Drag the orb onto the ✕ at the bottom to hide it until you talk to Jarvis in AntiGem again. Hidden during Antigravity voice calls.
strings.jarvis.settings.needsDisplayOverOtherApp: Needs “Display over other apps” for AntiGem.
strings.jarvis.settings.aSlimStatusLineCheckingT: A slim status line (“Checking the build…”) while it works.
strings.jarvis.settings.showWhatJarvisHeardAndSa: Show what Jarvis heard and said
strings.jarvis.settings.sendLiveContextWithEvery: Send live context with every message
strings.jarvis.settings.screenProjectChatOnScree: Screen, project, chat on screen, tasks, approvals and timers, so Jarvis rarely has to look them up.
strings.jarvis.settings.startAFreshChatAfterIdle: Start a fresh chat after idle time
strings.jarvis.settings.startAFreshChatAfterThis: Start a fresh chat after this many messages
strings.jarvis.settings.bothAreOffByDefaultSo: Both are off by default so Jarvis never forgets mid-task. A chat is only replaced when you speak the next message, never while it is working. You can always say “start again” or “new session”.
strings.jarvis.settings.aNewChatStartsWithThe: A new chat starts with the Jarvis memory note and the last lines of the old conversation.
strings.jarvis.settings.theNextMessageStartsANew: The next message starts a new Jarvis chat
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisMemoryJarvisCanEdi: Jarvis memory (Jarvis can edit this too)
strings.jarvis.settings.pIsAlreadyAOthernamePhra: “{p}” is already a {otherName} phrase. Remove it there first.
strings.jarvis.settings.addedPIsShortOrCommon: Added. “{p}” is short or common, so it only counts when said on its own after a short pause.
strings.jarvis.settings.addAWordOrAWhole: Add a word or a whole sentence
strings.jarvis.settings.readingFilesAndSearching: Reading files and searching is approved; anything else is read out and needs a yes.
strings.jarvis.settings.policyJarvisOwnToolsNeve: {policy} Jarvis' own tools never need approval. The chat on screen is only handled while hands-free mode is on (tasks always are).
strings.jarvis.settings.aHandsFreeAssistantForTh: A hands-free assistant for the whole app: talk to open projects and files, run and watch tasks, answer approvals, change settings, ask for help or your usage. Off by default; nothing listens until you turn it on.
strings.jarvis.settings.theJarvisChatsYouOpenedY: The Jarvis chats you opened yourself (New Jarvis chat) also show in All and the agent tabs; the voice chats Jarvis opens by itself stay under Jarvis.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisTalksToANormalHidd: Jarvis talks to a normal hidden chat of this agent (find it under Jarvis in the chat list). A fast model feels best for voice; big jobs run as tasks in their own chats.
strings.jarvis.settings.sentAfterAFixedPauseA: Sent after a fixed pause. A bar on the card fills while it counts down; tap Wait to keep talking.
strings.jarvis.settings.jarvisDecidesAfterDoneWa: Jarvis decides: after “Done, want me to run it?” the microphone opens; after “Saved the file.” it does not. Questions always open it.
strings.jarvis.settings.onlyAMessageThatStartsWi: Only a message that starts with one of your interrupt phrases (Voice shortcuts below) stops Jarvis' work; anything else waits.
strings.jarvis.settings.eachChatHasItsOwnVoice: Each chat has its own Voice switch on its strip; this is the default for new ones.
strings.jarvis.settings.aTurnThatWaitsSleepWait: A turn that waits (sleep, wait loops, wake-up timers) is stopped once news is waiting, or after 12 seconds while its tasks run; the news goes in at once.
strings.jarvis.settings.theNextMessageTellsItNot: The next message tells it not to wait; the news still waits until its turn ends.
strings.jarvis.settings.severalJarvisChatsCanWor: Several Jarvis chats can work at the same time. Each one runs and hears about only its own tasks; they never steer each other's work.
strings.jarvis.settings.themeChatFontSizeFloatin: Theme, chat font size, floating bubble and switcher, new-chat agent. Jarvis' own voice and listening options can always be changed by voice; approval and security settings never.
strings.jarvis.voice.theDevicesTextToSpeechIs: The device's text-to-speech is not available.
strings.jarvis.voice.noApiKeySetForThe: No API key set for the online voice; using the device voice.

strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.thisIsAnOlderV: This is an older version than the one installed. Older versions can have bugs that were fixed. Its data is kept.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.sameDeveloperA: Same developer as the installed version. Its data and permissions are kept.

strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.dataLeftByAnEa: Data left by an earlier app with this id will be deleted.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.newPermissions: New permissions it will ask for
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.theKeyIsSavedL: The key is saved, locked with this password, to Download/AntiGem on this phone: it stays there even if AntiGem is uninstalled. Then you can also send it to Drive or email. If the key is lost, apps signed with it can never be updated.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.youNeedThisPas: You need this password to restore the key (Developer key → Import) or to sign on a PC. Nobody can recover it.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.yourNameOrTeam: Your name or team, shown to people who install your apps.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.notBackedUpYet: Not backed up yet: Mini Apps keeps reminding you until it is
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.savedToShownKe: Saved to {shown}. Keep a second copy somewhere safe too.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.itIsNotBackedU: It is NOT backed up: back it up first, or it is lost for good.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.packagesYouExp: Packages you export are signed with your key. Anyone who installs one can only update it with a package signed by the same key.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstallUi.notBackedUpIfT: Not backed up. If this key is lost (AntiGem uninstalled, data cleared, phone lost), apps signed with it can never be updated.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstaller.thisPackageIsS: This package is signed by a different developer than the installed {optString} ({developer}, key {shortFingerprint}). Uninstall the installed app first; its data will be deleted.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstaller.aDevelopmentAp: A development app with the id {id} is in ~/mini-apps/{devFolder}. A package can't take its id (it would get that app's data): give the development app another id, or delete it, then install.
strings.miniapps.miniAppInstaller.itSharesDataWi: It shares data with the apps of "{sharedId}", and {name} there is signed by {developer} (key {shortFingerprint}), not by this package's developer. Only apps signed with the same key can share data.

strings.settings.egm.n1TheAgentFirstPointsOut:
1. The agent first points out risks and gaps in the task, then waits.
2. Type checklist: it writes a short plan (egm_lite_checklist.md).
3. Type goldfish: one fresh reviewer checks the plan (you can skip this).
4. Type exec: it makes the change.
5. Type review: one fresh reviewer checks the changes.
strings.settings.egm.whenAPlanOrDesignDocument: When a plan or design document already exists (yours, or written in another chat) and you want it checked before anyone builds it.
strings.settings.egm.theReviewersCheckTheDocumen: The reviewers check the document and the agent writes their findings into a report. Then you choose: the agent fixes the findings, you fix them yourself, or you stop there.
strings.settings.egm.normalChatClaudeCodeCodexTh: Normal chat (Claude Code, Codex, …): the agent does everything in that chat and runs the reviewers as its own hidden sub-agents. The simplest and lightest way. If the agent has no sub-agent tool, it stops and tells you to use a Jarvis chat.
strings.settings.egm.jarvisChatJarvisTabAJarvis: Jarvis chat (Jarvis tab → a Jarvis chat, then type the command): Jarvis manages the run. It starts a planner chat (or plans itself, see Jarvis below) and one chat per reviewer, which you can open from the chat list. The phases show as Jarvis' mission steps, and Jarvis asks you to approve the design. Use it to watch the reviewers, or when the agent has no sub-agent tool. Every reviewer chat is a full agent, so it needs more memory.
strings.settings.egm.sentAfterTheRunsFactsEgms: Sent after the run's facts (EGM's folder, the planner and reviewer goals, the limits). It tells Jarvis how to manage the planner and the reviewer chats.
strings.settings.egm.sentAfterTheRunsFactsEgms2: Sent after the run's facts (EGM's folder, the reviewers, the limits). It tells the agent how to run the reviewers in its own chat.
strings.settings.egm.googlesElephantGoldfishMode: Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model (open source, Apache 2.0). The agent (the Elephant) works out a design with you and writes it down. Then fresh reviewers (the Goldfish), who never saw your conversation, read only the document and try to break it. The design is fixed until it passes and you approve it; only then is code written.
strings.settings.egm.typeOneAtTheStartOf: Type one at the start of a message in any chat; the rest of the message is the task.
strings.settings.egm.n1TheAgentAsksYouQuestions:
1. The agent asks you questions until the idea is clear (brainstorm).
2. It writes the design document, section by section, and asks for your OK on each.
3. The reviewers attack the document; the agent fixes it or explains why a finding is wrong.
4. You approve the design.
5. Only then does it write the code.
strings.settings.egm.answerTheAgentsQuestionsItA:
• Answer the agent's questions: it asks one at a time.
• Everything is saved as files in your project, in {artifactDir}/<topic>/: the design document and every review report. Open them in Files.
• Nothing is coded before you approve. To approve, just say so; or ask for changes, or for one more review round.
• You can stop at any time. The files stay, and later you can check the document again with /egm-review.
strings.settings.egm.startWithQuickOrStandardRev:
• Start with Quick or Standard reviewers; Full runs eight reviewers in every round.
• If the phone gets slow, set Reviewers at the same time to 1.
• Write the task as you would explain it to a colleague: what, why, and any limits ("no new libraries").
• For a change of a few lines, a plain chat is cheaper than EGM.

Betas are early versions for testing new features, and they can have bugs.

Once a beta is installed you can't go back to the stable version until the next stable release (uninstalling would delete your data). Turning this off later stops new betas; you then get the next stable release as a normal update.

In chat, type /plu: to point the model at a plugin or one of its skills. Updating or reloading restarts that plugin's worker; its MCP connection and stored data are kept.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.theDesktopRunsInAnti: The desktop runs in AntiGem's terminal. Install it in Settings → Terminal & Shell, then come back here.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.antigemsOwnBuildOfTe: AntiGem's own build of Termux:X11, the app that shows the desktop. It runs inside AntiGem, so Android keeps the desktop running at full speed while you use it.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.thisTermuxX11DoesntS: This Termux:X11 doesn't share AntiGem's UID, so it can't run inside AntiGem. Uninstall it, then install it again.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.theOfficialTermuxX11: The official Termux:X11 is installed. It can't run inside AntiGem, and Android won't install AntiGem's build over it (they are signed differently). Uninstall it first, then install AntiGem's build.

strings.settings.x11Desktop.companionIsInstalled: {companion} is installed, but this Termux:X11 needs {neededCompanion}. Installing replaces it.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.xfceIsAFullLightDesk: XFCE is a full, light desktop and a good place to start.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.lxqtIsALightQtDeskto: LXQt is a light Qt desktop.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.itComesFromUbuntuApt: It comes from Ubuntu (apt) and runs in the Ubuntu chroot as your user. A large download.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.itComesFromX11RepoAn: It comes from x11-repo and is a large download.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.installsChromiumOrFi: Installs Chromium or Firefox in the Ubuntu chroot from the xtradeb/apps PPA (Ubuntu's own packages of both are snaps, which do not run in a chroot).
strings.settings.x11Desktop.installABrowserFromT: Install a browser from tur-repo to browse the web on your desktop.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.ifTheDesktopClosesBy: If the desktop closes by itself
strings.settings.x11Desktop.android12AndNewerSto: Android 12 and newer stop the extra processes of apps once there are more than 32 in total. A desktop starts many, so Android may close it. You can turn this limit off once, over ADB. It stays off until you turn it back on or reset the phone.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.connectTheTerminalsA: Connect the terminal's adb to this phone first.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.runLinuxDesktopAppsA: Run Linux desktop apps (a browser, an IDE, office apps) from AntiGem's terminal. Termux:X11 shows the desktop.
strings.settings.x11Desktop.theDesktopRunsInside: The desktop runs inside AntiGem, so Android won't slow it down or stop it while you use it.
